_about: The Enhanced lighting tune (src/Session/World/LightingTable.cs), read only under Enhanced graphics. Keyed chapter, then an optional mission folder, then weather zone ('ZONE1' to 'ZONE3' as the mission's weather.json authors them), e.g. {"C5": {"ZONE1": {"exposure": 1.1}, "M02": {"night": true, "ZONE1": {"sun_energy": 1.2}}}}. A chapter zone block holds only the fields that differ from the defaults; a mission zone block only those that differ from its chapter's. Any zone block may hold a 'clouds' and a 'gi' layer, sparse blocks of the same fields that apply over the resolved zone (chapter, then mission) while the Volumetric Clouds or Global Illumination option stands on; 'gi' applies after 'clouds', e.g. {"C1B": {"ZONE1": {"shadow_strength": 0.8, "clouds": {"god_rays": 1.5}, "gi": {"ambient_floor": 0.2, "sdfgi_energy": 0.6}}}}. A mission's 'night' flag makes it a moonlit mission (CONTEXT.md): every zone takes the night path, the capped energies and the light aimed at the dome's moon. The field names, ranges and meanings are ZoneLighting.Fields (src/Effects/ZoneLighting.cs). The lighting lab (Shift+F5 in --freecam) writes one zone's layer (gi while GI is on, else clouds while the clouds are, else the base block) and the mission's night flag here when run from the source tree; --debug-lighting=<field>:<value>,... overrides it for one launch. An empty file draws the untuned Enhanced look.
